g_policy.reason: The user opts in to the card, and the offer copy states the reward (priority routing, 60 minutes). The decline path leaves the menu, Upgrade and Billing unchanged, and the ad-failure path hides the card or shows a retry message.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 60 minutes of queue priority, which cannot be withdrawn, sold or transferred.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is an app event, returning to the profile menu from the Upgrade entry. It uses no chat content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The proposal removes nothing ("removes nothing free: yes"). Replies keep their normal speed if the user declines.

g_brand_safety.reason: The card sits in the s09 profile menu drawer, which is app chrome over a non-chat screen rated safe. It is not in the conversation and not next to unsafe or unknown content.

c1_revealed_value.reason: Priority routing is a charged resource. m02 and l02 list it as a Janitor+ subscriber benefit, so the existing-anchor test is met.

c2_evidence.reason: The claims about today's app rest on the model: Janitor+ sells priority routing (s02.e06, l02), s09.e31 is a permanent Upgrade entry, and m03 (inferred from s02.e07) supports free users having normal-priority routing. The new card, trigger and copy are the proposal's own additions, and its cost claim is a prediction.

c3_spares_payers.reason: A paid plan exists, but the proposal says subscribers already have priority routing and never see the card. The model shows no ad-removal benefit for the plan.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward is a 60-minute sample that ends, capped at 2 per day, so it grants no lasting access. The app already sells queue priority, so it does not take an unsold advantage from other users.

c5_moment.reason: The offer sits on the profile menu, a persistent surface the user chooses to open, and does not interrupt a task in progress.

c6_fits_simula.reason: It is a play-to-earn rewarded playable. The reward follows the verified play, and an unverified play gets no reward. The trigger is an app event.

c7_specific.reason: It names Janitor+'s priority routing, the profile menu drawer, and the Upgrade to Janitor Plus button (s09.e31), so it would not read the same in another app.

other_concern: The Upgrade entry's destination was not captured, so the "returns from Upgrade without subscribing" trigger is hard to detect. The placement is also ambiguous about whether the card shows permanently or only after a return. Free-tier queue behavior is only inferred (m03).
